Checking the summary against the code

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

The brief asks for a clearer review screen without losing capability. I followed a summary into the assigned PR’s code, chose three priorities, and compared four directions. I chose M to improve that route using the existing layers and PR content.

What I noticedWhat I changed
Six summary points share L49–130. I still have to find the lines behind each point.I gave each point a smaller target. The full wording and surrounding code stay available so I can check beyond the highlight.
The access check continues in another file.Inspect guard opens both checks. Return brings me back to the caller’s selection and reading position. I mapped this route manually.
File and display actions sit across several controls.I put file actions beside the filename and display settings above the code. Less-used tools sit in named menus, which adds a click.

Why I kept one code pane

Showing the caller and guard together squeezed both at laptop width, so I chose Return. Both comparison screens use Unified. The original fits more code; M gives files and summary links more room. Focus gives that space back.

What stays available

PR details, icons, layer numbers, J/K and Z Focus remain. Visiting a file leaves progress alone; Mark viewed and Undo change it. Full summary wording and secondary tools have named destinations. The capability map separates working interactions from previews; full functional parity is not implemented.

What I would test

I’d ask developers to explain the access check on both screens, then find something the summary might miss. I’d watch for wrong turns and missed branches. If smaller highlights lead people to overlook code, I’d change them.

Seven of 52 diffs at commit 23cdac2; manually mapped links. The PR is merged; Submit is disabled. Semantic diffs and modified-file review are outside this sample. No developer testing. This work exceeded the expected 1–2 hours.
